dossier.purpose: vLLM is a Python library and HTTP/gRPC server for LLM inference and serving (README.md:24), with C++/CUDA kernels (csrc/) and an optional Rust frontend (rust/). `vllm serve` hosts ONE model per process and exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints (completions, chat, responses, embeddings, audio), Anthropic Messages (/v1/messages), Cohere-style embed/rerank, pooling/score endpoints and a Prometheus /metrics endpoint (docs/serving/online_serving/README.md:5-93; docs/getting_started/quickstart.md:206). Facts bearing on the stated needs: (a) OTLP collector / privacy filter: none in this repo. Nothing receives or filters OTLP; vLLM only EXPORTS OTLP traces, and only when --otlp-traces-endpoint is set (vllm/tracing/otel.py:94-102). (b) Metrics store: none; metrics are exposed for Prometheus pull (vllm/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/metrics.py:56-82). (c) Events/logs store: none; logs go to stdout by default (vllm/envs.py:43) and no OTLP logs exporter exists. (d) Dashboards: no built-in UI; only example Grafana/Perses dashboards and a Prometheus+Grafana docker-compose (examples/observability/dashboards/README.md:8-39; examples/observability/prometheus_grafana/docker-compose.yaml:4-19). (e) Trace/dataset/experiment store: none; `vllm bench serve|throughput|latency|sweep` replays datasets and can save JSON results (docs/benchmarking/cli.md:61-86,194-222), and traces can be exported to an external backend such as Jaeger (examples/observability/opentelemetry/README.md:5-37). (f) Local model server: yes, that is its function; documented Claude Code and Codex configurations exist (docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md; docs/serving/integrations/codex.md); default builds include CUDA SM 8.9 (CMakeLists.txt:116-132). (g) Semantic code search: none; there is no indexer, chunker, vector store or query layer. It can serve embedding models (/v1/embeddings, /v2/embed, /pooling: vllm/entrypoints/pooling/embed/api_router.py:28-47; vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/api_router.py:27-39), and its RAG docs use an external Milvus through LangChain/LlamaIndex (docs/deployment/frameworks/retrieval_augmented_generation.md:7-8).

claims.claim: vLLM is a fast and easy-to-use library for LLM inference and serving.
OpenAI-compatible API server, plus Anthropic Messages API and gRPC support
Tool calling and reasoning parsers; structured outputs using xgrammar or guidance
Support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel GPUs, and x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs; hardware plugins such as Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, IBM Spyre, Huawei Ascend, Rebellions NPU, Apple Silicon, MetaX GPU
Quantization: FP8, MXFP8/MXFP4, NVFP4, INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, TorchAO, and more
Continuous batching of incoming requests, chunked prefill, prefix caching
Speculative decoding including n-gram, suffix, EAGLE, DFlash
Embedding and retrieval models (e.g., E5-Mistral, GTE, ColBERT)
vLLM seamlessly supports 200+ model architectures on Hugging Face
Install vLLM with uv (recommended) or pip (`uv pip install vllm`), or build from source for development
For security disclosures, use GitHub Security Advisories
ABSENCE: the README says nothing about usage-data collection/telemetry, OTLP/observability, or Claude Code/Codex; those appear only in docs/

install.method: uv venv + automatic PyTorch backend selection (NVIDIA CUDA docs)
install.command:
uv venv --python 3.12 --seed
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto
docker run --runtime nvidia --gpus all -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface --env "HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN" -p 8000:8000 --ipc=host vllm/vllm-openai:latest --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B

install.method: Specific CUDA-variant wheel from GitHub Releases (documented command resolves releases/latest, not a pinned tag)
install.command:
export VLLM_VERSION=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/vllm-project/vllm/releases/latest | jq -r .tag_name | sed 's/^v//')
export CUDA_VERSION=130 # or other
export CPU_ARCH=$(uname -m) # x86_64 or aarch64
uv pip install "https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/download/v${VLLM_VERSION}/vllm-${VLLM_VERSION}+cu${CUDA_VERSION}-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_${CPU_ARCH}.whl" --extra-index-url "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu${CUDA_VERSION}"

install.method: Source build, Python-only with precompiled kernels (full compile alternative: `uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto`, gpu.cuda.inc.md:153-157)
install.command:
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
cd vllm
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install --editable . --torch-backend=auto

install.method: macOS Apple Silicon CPU backend, build from source (experimental)
install.command:
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
cd vllm
uv pip install -r requirements/cpu.txt
uv pip install -e .

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - docs: OS Linux, Python 3.10-3.13 (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.md:27-28; pyproject.toml:35 allows <3.15); pre-built abi3 wheels cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64 (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:46); Docker image vllm/vllm-openai (gpu.cuda.inc.md:265-276); release pipeline builds x86_64 CUDA 13.0/12.9 and CPU wheels (.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:44-56,139-165).
platforms.wsl2: yes (not first-class) - no native Windows; docs say use WSL with a Linux distribution (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.md:31); setup.py:88-90 says 'Linux platform (including WSL)'; code special-cases WSL2: pinned memory off by default, opt in with VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1 (vllm/platforms/cuda.py:307-327; vllm/envs.py:2066-2071), multiprocessing forced to spawn (vllm/utils/system_utils.py:153-154), pinned-memory warning for CPU offload + CUDA graphs (vllm/platforms/cuda.py:357-376). No WSL job found in .github/ or .buildkite/.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes, CPU backend only and experimental - 'experimental support for macOS with Apple Silicon', build from source, FP32/FP16 (docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.apple.inc.md:4-6); VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE forced to cpu on macOS (setup.py:85-87); GPU acceleration is the separate community plugin vllm-metal (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.apple.inc.md:4-9). CI: daily smoke test on macos-15 (required) and macos-26 (non-blocking) (.github/workflows/macos-smoke-test.yml:17-27). Docs say no pre-built Apple wheels (cpu.apple.inc.md:28) but the release pipeline builds a macOS arm64 CPU wheel (.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:96-133).
platforms.gpu: yes - NVIDIA CUDA compute capability >= 7.5 (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:9); default builds include SM 8.9 (Ada; docs/features/quantization/README.md:79 maps Ada to SM 8.9): CMakeLists.txt:116-132, docker/Dockerfile:293, .buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:10; FP8 W8A8 needs CC >= 8.9 (docs/features/quantization/llm_compressor/fp8.md:16). The only in-code RTX 4090 mention is a shared-memory table in vendored flash-linear-attention (vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/utils.py:179-183). Also AMD ROCm, Intel XPU, TPU via separate vllm-tpu (docs/getting_started/quickstart.md:77-86). Caveats: default wheels/images target CUDA 13.0 (vllm/envs.py:90; docker/Dockerfile:25), which needs R580+ drivers (gpu.cuda.inc.md:327); CUDA forward-compat libs are unsupported on GeForce (vllm/env_override.py:58-60); no GeForce/RTX runner in .buildkite (CI GPUs: L4, A100, H100, H200, B200, AMD MI-series).

integrations.cli: yes - `vllm` console script (pyproject.toml:43-44) with subcommands serve, chat, complete, launch, bench, collect-env, run-batch (vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py:55-62; docs/cli/README.md:12). Separate Rust binary `vllm-rs` (rust/src/cmd/src/main.rs:85-218), opt-in via VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 (vllm/envs.py:1394-1402), and a Rust `vllm-bench` client (rust/src/bench/README.md:3-10).
integrations.mcp: No MCP server found. vLLM is an MCP CLIENT for tool servers: `--tool-server host:port[,...]|demo` feeds the Responses API through an SSE MCP client (vllm/entrypoints/launchers/cli_args.py:120-126; vllm/entrypoints/mcp/tool_server.py:20-30,104-120; docs/usage/security.md:292-296). `mcp>=2.0.0,<3.0.0` is a hard dependency (requirements/common.txt:54).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK: `from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams, PoolingParams, AsyncLLMEngine, ...` (vllm/__init__.py:16-28,76-101; docs/getting_started/quickstart.md:112-142). HTTP: OpenAI-compatible /v1/completions, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses (+retrieve/cancel), /v1/embeddings, /v1/audio/*, /v1/models (docs/serving/online_serving/openai_compatible_server.md:16-35; vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/api_router.py:48-117); Anthropic /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens (vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py:51-119); Cohere-style /v2/embed, /v2/rerank (docs/serving/online_serving/README.md:30-37); /pooling, /classify, /score (README.md:39-55; vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/api_router.py:27-39); /metrics, /health, /version, /load (README.md:80-93). Optional gRPC via `--grpc` needs `pip install vllm[grpc]` (vllm/entrypoints/launchers/grpc_server.py:27-40; setup.py:1537-1538). Default bind: all interfaces, port 8000 (vllm/entrypoints/launchers/cli_args.py:260-262; vllm/entrypoints/launchers/launcher.py:275).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Documented, both via the HTTP API only (no plugin, hook or MCP server). Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 plus ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (any value) and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL=<served-model-name>, then run `claude`; vLLM must run with --enable-auto-tool-choice and a --tool-call-parser; served model names containing '/' do not work (docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md:13,25-33,39-58,80). Codex: ~/.codex/config.toml with model_provider='vllm', [model_providers.vllm] base_url='http://localhost:8000/v1', wire_api='responses', env_key VLLM_API_KEY (any value) (docs/serving/integrations/codex.md:38-61). Code support: the Anthropic handler drops Claude Code's x-anthropic-billing-header system block so prefix caching keeps working (vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:237-241,259-271); Responses router at vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/api_router.py:48-77. Neither page covers Claude Code/Codex telemetry (OTLP): vLLM neither receives nor forwards it. AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are instructions for AI agents contributing to vLLM's own source, not a runtime integration (AGENTS.md:1-4; CLAUDE.md:1).

readme.telemetry_and_network: (1) Outbound usage telemetry is ON by default: vLLM POSTs a usage record to https://stats.vllm.ai at startup and every 600 s (vllm/envs.py:812-814; vllm/usage/usage_lib.py:166-173,248-271), started from rank 0 of the GPU/XPU worker (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:490-492; vllm/v1/worker/xpu_worker.py:198). Fields: random uuid, cloud-provider guess, CPU model/count/family, RAM, platform string, GPU count/type/memory, CUDA/XPU runtime, model architecture class name, vLLM version, 5 env-var values, plus engine knobs such as dtype, TP/DP/PP sizes, max_model_len, quantization, attention backend, spec-decode method (usage_lib.py:129-151,232-235; vllm/v1/utils.py:730-771); no prompt/response field appears in the code. A copy is appended to ~/.config/vllm/usage_stats.json (usage_lib.py:273-278). Opt-out: VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or VLLM_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (only the literal value 1 counts), or an empty ~/.config/vllm/do_not_track file (vllm/envs.py:815-823; usage_lib.py:50-68; docs/usage/usage_stats.md:52-61). The main docker/Dockerfile does not set it; only docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le sets VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 (docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le:86). (2) Model/tokenizer downloads from Hugging Face Hub unless HF_HUB_OFFLINE is set (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:841; vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:178,376,440,487); HF_TOKEN only for gated models (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:269-274). No vLLM account is required. (3) If the flashinfer-cubin package is absent (it is dropped from published wheel metadata, setup.py:1323-1327), vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:563-588 does an HTTP GET (5 s timeout) to an NVIDIA artifactory (flashinfer.py:77-80) when TRTLLM-attention support is evaluated (flashinfer.py:603-604). (4) Install/build-time network: PyPI, PyTorch indices, https://flashinfer.ai/whl/ (requirements/cuda.txt:16), wheels.vllm.ai/GitHub for precompiled builds, CUTLASS fetched from GitHub in source builds (gpu.cuda.inc.md:204). (5) Tracing is opt-in: OTLP trace export only when --otlp-traces-endpoint is set (gRPC by default with insecure=True; http/protobuf via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL) (vllm/config/observability.py:36-37; vllm/tracing/otel.py:94-102); spans carry request id, token counts, latencies and temperature/top_p/max_tokens/n, not prompt text (vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:806-842). Metrics are Prometheus pull at /metrics (vllm/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/metrics.py:56-82). No OTLP receiver, OTLP metrics/logs exporter, or other phone-home beyond (1)-(3) was found; the Rust frontend only installs a stderr log subscriber (rust/src/tracing/src/lib.rs:31-47). (6) Prompt/response content is logged only with --enable-log-requests (DEBUG shows prompt text/token ids) and --enable-log-outputs, both default off (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:3012-3020; vllm/entrypoints/launchers/cli_args.py:150-153). (7) The server listens on all interfaces, port 8000, by default (vllm/entrypoints/launchers/launcher.py:275,287). The Swagger /docs page needs internet unless --enable-offline-docs (docs/serving/online_serving/README.md:95-101).

entry_points.what: console script `vllm` -> vllm.entrypoints.cli.main:main (vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py:39-108); subcommands serve, chat, complete, launch, bench, collect-env, run-batch
`vllm serve` (ServeSubcommand) -> launchers/api_server/entry.py:163-176 run_server -> uvicorn/FastAPI; --grpc branch needs vllm[grpc]; Rust frontend when VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
registers API routers by supported task (generate, pooling, transcription/realtime, scale-out) and dev routes when VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
Python SDK lazy exports: LLM (offline API), AsyncLLMEngine, SamplingParams, PoolingParams
`vllm-rs` binary: serve (managed Python headless engine + Rust frontend), frontend, bench serve, render
init_otel_tracer: OTLP trace exporter setup, invoked by AsyncLLM/LLMEngine only when --otlp-traces-endpoint is set (vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:125-127)

code.architecture: Python package vllm/ (2,479 .py files), C++/CUDA csrc/ (308 files, built via CMakeLists.txt and cmake/), Rust workspace rust/ (16 crates, 329 .rs files). Process model: API-server process(es) -> engine-core process(es) over ZMQ -> one GPU worker per GPU (docs/design/arch_overview.md:67-117). Key modules: vllm/entrypoints/ (cli/, launchers/api_server, openai/, anthropic/, cohere/, pooling/, serve/instrumentator (metrics, health), speech_to_text/, scale_out/, mcp/); vllm/v1/engine/ (async_llm.py, core.py, core_client.py, output_processor.py); vllm/v1/core/ (sched/scheduler.py, kv_cache_manager.py, block_pool.py); vllm/v1/worker/ (gpu_worker.py, gpu_model_runner.py, cpu_worker.py); vllm/v1/executor/, vllm/v1/attention/, vllm/v1/spec_decode/, vllm/v1/kv_offload/, vllm/v1/metrics/ (Prometheus loggers, stat-logger plugins); vllm/model_executor/ (models/registry.py, layers/quantization/); vllm/compilation/ (torch.compile passes); vllm/config/ (pydantic configs incl. observability.py); vllm/platforms/ (cuda.py, rocm.py, cpu.py, xpu.py, tpu.py, zen_cpu.py); vllm/tool_parsers/ and vllm/reasoning/ (per-model parsers); vllm/tracing/ (OTel traces); vllm/usage/usage_lib.py (usage telemetry); vllm/plugins/ (entry-point groups general, platform, io_processor, stat_logger, endpoint: docs/design/plugin_system.md:46-56); vllm/benchmarks/ (`vllm bench`). Rust: rust/src/{cmd,server,chat,parser,tokenizer,engine-core-client,metrics,llm,managed-engine,bench,mock-engine,tracing} plus rust/proto/*.proto.
code.packaging_and_release: Build: setuptools + setuptools-scm (git-derived version) + CMake extensions + setuptools-rust (pyproject.toml:1-14; setup.py:1505-1551); abi3 wheels built with --py-limited-api=cp38 (docker/Dockerfile:655); `vllm-rs` binary shipped inside the wheel (setup.py:1469-1474). Artifacts: PyPI wheels (default variant = CUDA 13.0, no local-version suffix: vllm/envs.py:90; setup.py:1263-1272; docker/Dockerfile:668), additional CUDA 12.9 / CPU / XPU / macOS arm64 CPU wheels staged to S3 and wheel indices (.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:27-209), Docker Hub images vllm/vllm-openai and variants pushed as user vllmbot via DOCKERHUB_TOKEN (release-pipeline.yaml:1128-1169), crates.io crate vllm-proto via OIDC trusted publishing (.github/workflows/proto-crate.yml:50-70), Buf schema pushes (.github/workflows/buf.yml:39-57). Process: release builds run on Buildkite, triggered by RC tags; the final vX.Y.Z tag does not trigger a build (RELEASE.md:21-24); cadence goal ~2 weeks (RELEASE.md:7). PyPI upload is a manual-gated Buildkite step using twine and a PYPI_TOKEN secret, labelled 'experimental, use with caution' (release-pipeline.yaml:1171-1189; .buildkite/scripts/upload-release-wheels-pypi.sh:31-38,78-79); only wheels without '+' in the filename go to PyPI (upload-release-wheels-pypi.sh:71-72). Integrity: no cosign/sigstore/GPG signing, SLSA provenance or PyPI attestations found (grep over .buildkite, .github, docker, tools, docs/contributing; only apt GPG-key handling in docker/Dockerfile); sha256sum is used for build-cache keys and macOS wheel transfer checks (docker/Dockerfile:659; release-pipeline.yaml:106,125-129). Release builds can assert a clean tagged checkout via GIT_REPO_CHECK -> tools/check_repo.sh (docker/Dockerfile:627-629; tools/check_repo.sh:4-14) and enforce a 500 MB wheel size (docker/Dockerfile:668-679). Docs link GitHub Release wheel assets (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:46) but no workflow uploading them was found in the repo.
code.tests_and_ci: pytest (pyproject.toml:107-118 markers). About 1,566 test_*.py files under tests/ (1,876 .py files incl. conftest/helpers; 37 conftest.py), e.g. tests/entrypoints/{anthropic,openai/responses,pooling/embed}, tests/tracing, tests/v1/tracing, tests/kernels, tests/models, tests/distributed, tests/evals. Rust: 195 .rs files contain #[test]/#[cfg(test)] blocks (expect-test snapshots, cargo nextest preferred: rust/AGENTS.md:31-37). CI: 12 GitHub Actions workflows in .github/workflows/ (pre-commit [ruff, typos, clang-format, markdownlint, actionlint, shellcheck, mypy 3.10-3.13, SPDX/header, cargo fmt/sort checks per .pre-commit-config.yaml], macos-smoke-test [daily; builds CPU wheel, serves Qwen3-0.6B with dummy weights, hits /health and /v1/completions], buf, proto-crate [semver check + publish], run-ci-command [triggers Buildkite from PR comments], plus labeling/PR-bot/stale/approval workflows; most gated on github.repository_owner == vllm-project). The real test suites run on Buildkite: .buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml (36 files; GPUs L4, A100, H100, H200, B200 and AMD MI250/MI300/MI355), .buildkite/hardware_tests/ (AMD, Ascend NPU, CPU, GH200, Intel), .buildkite/image_build/, ci_config.yaml; .buildkite/test-pipeline.yaml is a deprecated stub. Relevant jobs: Metrics/Tracing (.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:355-383), anthropic and responses entrypoints (.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:130-157), Rust frontend cargo/E2E (rust_frontend_cargo.yaml, rust_frontend.yaml). No RTX 4090/GeForce or WSL2 job found. Dependabot covers GitHub Actions and pip (.github/dependabot.yml).
code.dependencies: Python (setup.py:1293-1345 feeds install_requires): requirements/common.txt = 58 direct requirements (fastapi[standard], starlette, pydantic, transformers>=5.10.4, huggingface_hub, openai, anthropic, mcp, prometheus_client, opentelemetry-sdk/api/exporter-otlp/semantic-conventions-ai, pyzmq, xgrammar, llguidance, protobuf, python-json-logger, ...); requirements/cuda.txt adds 18 (torch==2.13.0, torchaudio, torchvision, flashinfer-python==0.6.18.post1, flashinfer-cubin [dropped from wheel metadata], nvidia-cutlass-dsl, tilelang, numba, ...; extra index https://flashinfer.ai/whl/); cpu.txt adds 9; rocm.txt 19; xpu.txt 17; tpu.txt 11; kv_connectors.txt 4. Build: pyproject.toml [build-system].requires = 9 (torch == 2.13.0 pinned), requirements/build/cuda.txt 12, build/rust.txt 4. Tests: requirements/test/cuda.in ~60 direct, requirements/test/cuda.txt ~369 pins; docs.in 14; lint.txt 1. setup.py declares 15 optional extras (zen, bench, tensorizer, fastsafetensors, instanttensor, runai, audio, video, deepstream, flashinfer, b12x, helion, grpc, otel, extra-quant) (setup.py:1511-1548). Rust: rust/Cargo.toml = 16 member crates, 120 workspace dependencies (107 external + 13 path crates), rust/Cargo.lock present, git dependencies llm-multimodal and oss-harmony (rust/Cargo.toml:64,70). CUTLASS is fetched at build time (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:204).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: private reporting via GitHub Security Advisories, severity tiers, embargo for CRITICAL/HIGH, CVE after fix merge, prenotification group (SECURITY.md:3-76). Threat model: docs/usage/security.md; vulnerability management team: docs/contributing/vulnerability_management.md.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:49 - OpenAI-compatible API server, plus Anthropic Messages API and gRPC support
claim_checks.evidence: Anthropic: POST /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens (vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py:51-119), tested in CI (.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml:130-136). gRPC exists but is optional: import fails unless vllm[grpc] (smg-grpc-servicer) is installed (vllm/entrypoints/launchers/grpc_server.py:27-40; setup.py:1537-1538), and docs call it insecure by default (docs/usage/security.md:352-356).

claim_checks.claim: docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md:13,64 - vLLM implements the Anthropic Messages API; Claude Code's per-request attribution hash in the system prompt (which defeats prefix caching) is handled automatically in vLLM > 0.17.1
claim_checks.evidence: vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py:237-241 skips system text blocks starting with x-anthropic-billing-header; inline system messages are stripped the same way (:259-271); unit tests at tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py:424-443.

risks: Network/security defaults: `vllm serve` binds all interfaces on port 8000 (host default None -> '' bind) with no auth unless --api-key, and CORS allows all origins (vllm/entrypoints/launchers/cli_args.py:260-262,291; vllm/entrypoints/launchers/launcher.py:275,287). --api-key covers only /v1, /v2, /inference (and /cohere) prefixes; /invocations, /pooling, /classify, /score, /rerank, /tokenize, /detokenize, /health, /version, /load stay open (docs/usage/security.md:146-218). gRPC, torch.distributed and KV-transfer ports are unauthenticated by design (security.md:5-44,352-372); VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE and endpoint plugins can expose arbitrary RPC (security.md:226-237,339-350). Mitigations: --host, --uds, reverse proxy (security.md:272-278).

Default-on outbound telemetry to https://stats.vllm.ai (startup + every 10 min); opt-out works only for the literal value 1 or a do_not_track file; the main Docker image does not set it (vllm/usage/usage_lib.py:50-68,248-271; vllm/envs.py:812-823; only docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le:86 sets it). Extra unprompted GET to an NVIDIA artifactory when flashinfer-cubin is absent (vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:563-588) and Hugging Face Hub access unless HF_HUB_OFFLINE (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:841).

Observability scope is narrow for an OTLP-based pipeline: OTLP export is traces only (no metrics/logs), the gRPC exporter hard-codes insecure=True, spans exist only with --otlp-traces-endpoint, and the Rust frontend rejects that flag (vllm/tracing/otel.py:21-26,94-102; vllm/config/observability.py:36-39; rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs:320-326). Prompt/response text can enter logs with --enable-log-requests (DEBUG) or --enable-log-outputs (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:3012-3020; vllm/entrypoints/launchers/cli_args.py:150-153), so privacy filtering would have to happen downstream.

Hardware/platform fit: default wheel/image targets CUDA 13.0, which needs R580+ drivers, while install docs still say CUDA 12.9 (vllm/envs.py:90; docker/Dockerfile:25; docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:4,327); CUDA forward-compat libs are unsupported on GeForce (vllm/env_override.py:58-60); no GeForce/RTX 4090 or WSL2 job in CI and release performance validation covers only H100 and MI300x (RELEASE.md:45-49; .buildkite/test_areas device list); WSL2 needs special handling (vllm/platforms/cuda.py:307-327).

Operational scope: one model per server process (docs/usage/faq.md:3-5; vllm/config/model.py:135-137), so a chat/coding model plus an embedding model means two instances on two ports (docs/deployment/frameworks/retrieval_augmented_generation.md:25-36); gpu_memory_utilization defaults to 0.92 per instance, so co-hosting needs explicit fractions (vllm/config/cache.py:103-110); at least 2+N physical CPU cores and a busy-loop engine process (docs/configuration/optimization.md:426-441); tool calling needs per-model parser flags (docs/serving/integrations/claude_code.md:33).

Supply chain/release hygiene: no artifact signing, SLSA provenance or PyPI attestations found (grep of .buildkite, .github, docker, tools, docs/contributing); PyPI upload is a manual Buildkite step with a long-lived PYPI_TOKEN, labelled 'experimental, use with caution' (.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml:1174; .buildkite/scripts/upload-release-wheels-pypi.sh:31-38,78-79); GitHub-release asset upload not found in repo although docs link to it (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:46; RELEASE.md:24). Heavy pinned stack: torch==2.13.0 in build and runtime, flashinfer from an extra index (pyproject.toml:10; requirements/cuda.txt:7,16-18). Cache directories are loaded without integrity checks, including code-executing formats (docs/usage/security.md:374-378).

Maintenance/API churn: releases roughly every 2 weeks with minor-version breaking changes; back-compat guaranteed only for a limited number of minors (RELEASE.md:7,15; docs/contributing/deprecation_policy.md:13-19); deprecation shims already present (vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py:24-30; vllm/entrypoints/grpc_server.py:7-13); experimental/early features: GGUF moved out-of-tree and 'highly experimental' (docs/features/quantization/gguf.md:3-7), macOS CPU 'experimental' (docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.apple.inc.md:4), Rust frontend 'very early stage' with unsupported flags (rust/AGENTS.md:3; rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs:14-35).

Scope/licensing/evidence gaps: the repo has no OTLP collector, metrics/log store, dashboard app, experiment/dataset store or code-search index (see purpose); Apache-2.0 overall (LICENSE; pyproject.toml:19-20) with bundled third-party code under other terms (MIT: vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/LICENSE:1-3; NVIDIA BSD-style header: vllm/third_party/pynvml.py:6-32); docs note optional deps are kept out of images to avoid license issues (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md:297-298); published performance numbers are project-authored, hardware is often unspecified, and no independent third-party benchmark is cited in the repo.

checks.statement: Anonymous usage data is collected by default (verified: yes): POSTed to https://stats.vllm.ai at start and every 600 s; opt out via VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS, DO_NOT_TRACK (or VLLM_DO_NOT_TRACK) with literal value '1' only, or ~/.config/vllm/do_not_track; docs sample is 'as of v0.4.0' while code sends more fields; README silent
checks.note: is_usage_stats_enabled() returns True unless an opt-out is set. report_usage_stats() runs on rank 0 at GPU-worker init and starts a daemon thread. That thread appends to usage_stats.json, POSTs to VLLM_USAGE_STATS_SERVER (default https://stats.vllm.ai), then sleeps 600 s and repeats. VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS and VLLM_DO_NOT_TRACK/DO_NOT_TRACK are compared with == '1'. usage_stats.md:11 says 'as of v0.4.0', and v1/utils.py:733-770 adds DP/PP size, max_model_len, attention_backend, spec_decode_method and more. README.md has no telemetry mention. Extra precision the dossier doesn't state: a non-'1' VLLM_DO_NOT_TRACK value masks DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (envs.py:816-823), and the do_not_track path follows VLLM_CONFIG_ROOT/XDG_CONFIG_HOME (envs.py:335-339,686-691).
